answer: Pin each agent to one camera sensor. Every sensor carries a unique noise pattern no two chips share. First, the agent photographs a challenge card and the network keeps only the noise hash. Second, one hash anchors one agent, and a second binding is refused at once. Third, a random recheck each quarter demands a fresh photo in ten minutes, and a miss burns a 250 POA bond and freezes the identity 30 days. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 sensors at $150 a phone, $150,000. A fake without its own sensor is a vine with no wharf to climb, and the atlas of fakes falls apart at the first check.
